key_insight: A variationally correct first-order least-squares residual makes physics-informed operator learning locally reliable by linking training loss to error in the PDE-compliant norm.
engineering_relevance: For compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, this approach supports finite-element-compatible neural surrogates with a physics-based error indicator at inference.
method: Establish residual–error equivalence using linearized stability and Lipschitz continuity of the residual derivative.
Train a reduced-basis neural operator in a conforming finite element space, using solution snapshots only to construct the basis.
Assemble the residual loss and its symbolically derived gradient with a finite element library.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show that the square root of loss excess tracks error and that the operator outperforms grid-based baselines in the PDE-compliant norm when evaluated in the same finite element space.
watch_item: Residual–error guarantees depend on PDE-specific stability and regularity conditions and may hold only near a solution branch.
paper_title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
